name: FIFTY-SIX (AMBATHIYAARU)
description: Fifty-Six (56), known locally as 'Ambathiyaaru', is a complex and highly strategic trick-taking card game popular in the Kerala region of India. An expansion of the simpler game '28', it is played with a double deck of cards and a specialized point-count system from the Jass family. The game is known for its intense bidding phase and the use of 'tables' (physical cards from the unused portion of the deck) to keep track of match scores. It is a partnership game that demands precise card counting and team-wide tactical coordination.

content.text: Fifty-Six (56), known locally as 'Ambathiyaaru', is a complex and highly strategic trick-taking card game popular in the Kerala region of India. An expansion of the simpler game '28', it is played with a double deck of cards and a specialized point-count system from the Jass family. The game is known for its intense bidding phase and the use of 'tables' (physical cards from the unused portion of the deck) to keep track of match scores. It is a partnership game that demands precise card counting and team-wide tactical coordination.

Fifty-Six is a South Asian adaptation of the Dutch Jass family of games. It likely reached the Kerala coast through historical trade connections. It evolved from the 28-card variant to include more cards and a higher total point count (56) to accommodate larger groups of players.
4, 6, or 8 players in two fixed teams. Partners sit alternately.
Two standard decks stripped of all cards below 9. Total 48 cards (A, K, Q, J, 10, 9 of each suit, twice). For 8 players, Sevens and Eights are added (Total 64).
Two standard decks stripped of all cards below 9. Total 48 cards (A, K, Q, J, 10, 9 of each suit, twice). For 8 players, Sevens and Eights are added (Total 64).
Cards are dealt in three rounds: 8 cards per player initially. Bidding occurs during the dealing process.

items.text: Forced bid: If you are the last player of the non-dealer's team to bid and everyone before you has passed, you must bid at least 28. By the time the bidding reaches the dealer, there has always been at least one bid.
Throw in with no points: If any player has no points (hand consists entirely of Kings and Queens), the cards are thrown in and redealt by the same dealer.
Throw in with all Jacks: If one player is dealt all eight Jacks, the cards must be thrown in and redealt by the same dealer.
Alternative scoring (40–56): Bids from 40 to 55 win 2 or lose 3 tables; a bid of 56 wins 3 or loses 4.
Alternative scoring (40–48): Bids from 40 to 48 win 2 or lose 3 tables; all bids of 49 or more win 3 or lose 4.
Redouble times three: When a bid is redoubled, the basic table score is multiplied by 3 rather than 4.

Cot: If the winning team wins all the tricks they win twice the usual number of tables. Opponents can offer to surrender before the end of play; if accepted, the winning side gets the ordinary number of tables. If they play on and win all tricks they get double; if they lose any trick they lose double the usual number.
